correctness.rationale: The 16 even-weight five-bit representatives, Hamming-distance-four adjacency and all common-neighbor counts identify precisely the degree-five Clebsch graph. Exhaustive membership testing of 65,535 nonempty vertex masks gives 392 faces with \(f=(16,80,160,120,16)\), 40 maximal tetrahedra, and 16 maximal 4-simplices. The staged toggle algorithm pairs 191 disjoint cover relations, leaving exactly one critical vertex and nine critical dimension-three cells. An independently constructed directed Hasse graph contains all 1,200 nonempty cover incidences and is exhaustively topologically sorted, proving acyclicity. Forman discrete Morse theory yields a CW complex with a single 0-cell and nine 3-cells; each attaches to a point, proving wedge of nine \(S^3\), and the integral homology conclusion. Distinct face-recursion computation confirms f-vector and mod-two ranks (15,65,95,16). No infinite extrapolation or unproved attaching-map degree is needed.

value.rationale: The 16-vertex folded five-cube is a canonical and highly symmetric triangle-free strongly regular graph, naturally also named the degree-five Clebsch or Greenwood–Gleason graph. Its independence complex is a nonpure 4-dimensional flag complex, and determining its full integral homotopy type—not merely first-homology vanishing or Euler characteristic—is a natural topological invariant of this independently motivated object. The rank-nine sphere bouquet resolves exact attaching-map and torsion information beyond the applicable suspension theorem and the 2026 first-homology result. The modest finite size enables complete reproducible proof; no broad downstream impact is asserted.
